title: What randomness survives in macroscopic fracture of a random solid?
summary: Random fracture energies can homogenize to deterministic limits, yet strength, crack initiation, path, and finite-size failure statistics may remain sample-dependent. Which fracture observables self-average, and which retain irreducible randomness?

statement.lead: For a stationary random brittle medium, stochastic homogenization can yield a deterministic effective free-discontinuity energy under ergodicity. Let Q_epsilon^omega denote a fracture observable such as initiation load, peak strength, crack path, or quasistatic evolution. The residual question is
equations: Q_\varepsilon^\omega\ \xrightarrow[\varepsilon\to0]{\ ?\ }\ Q_{\mathrm{eff}}\quad\text{or a nontrivial limiting probability law}.
statement.after: The open target is to determine, for specified random ensembles and fracture models, which macroscopic failure observables become deterministic, how fast fluctuations decay when they do, and when randomness survives the homogenized energy.

why: Heterogeneous solids can have nearly deterministic effective elastic properties while failure remains controlled by rare weak regions, localization, and extreme fluctuations. Fracture therefore tests the limits of ordinary representative-volume reasoning.

The distinction matters for concrete, rocks, ceramics, composites, porous solids, additively manufactured materials, and other structures whose reliability depends on tails and sample-to-sample variability rather than only mean stiffness.
A rigorous answer would clarify when a deterministic effective fracture law is sufficient and when a stochastic mesoscale or probabilistic description remains essential.
scope: Primary setting: stationary or ergodic random brittle and quasi-brittle media with a clear scale separation between microstructural correlation length and specimen size; quasistatic loading is the initial focus.
The page distinguishes homogenization of the static fracture energy from convergence of strength, initiation, crack geometry, and crack evolution. These are different mathematical statements.

Dynamic fragmentation, fatigue, corrosion-assisted fracture, and randomness generated by unresolved manufacturing history are outside the core statement unless explicitly incorporated into the random ensemble.

boundary.text: Representative- and statistical-volume concepts are mature for random elastic media, but localization and softening complicate their extension to failure; studies of quasi-brittle media have long shown that an ordinary elastic-style RVE may cease to be representative once damage localizes.

Static stochastic fracture energy can homogenize rigorously. Cagnetti, Dal Maso, Scardia and Zeppieri prove stochastic homogenization of broad free-discontinuity functionals, with deterministic effective densities under ergodicity.

Effective fracture resistance can also be derived in specific disordered brittle systems. Lebihain and co-workers obtain an effective toughness framework by homogenizing crack-front interactions with toughness disorder.

Finite statistical-volume studies nevertheless report that fracture strength can remain random, anisotropic, and size-dependent at scales where elastic response has already become effectively homogeneous. This is evidence about finite-size observables, not a contradiction of energy homogenization.

Evolutionary homogenization is known in important special settings. Negri proves homogenization of Griffith evolution for periodic brittle laminates with a prescribed crack path, showing that some crack-evolution problems do admit an effective deterministic description.

Recent rigorous work continues to extend stochastic homogenization of fracture-type surface energies, including random functionals on asymptotically piecewise-rigid deformations. A general quantitative theory connecting these effective energies to strength fluctuations, nucleation, unrestricted crack paths, and full random quasistatic evolution remains incomplete.

settle: For a stated random ensemble and fracture model, characterize the limiting behavior of declared observables such as initiation load, peak strength, effective toughness, crack geometry, or quasistatic evolution: deterministic limit, nontrivial stochastic limit, or lack of self-averaging.

Where deterministic limits exist, a quantitative result should identify the scale dependence of fluctuations or convergence. Where randomness survives, the limiting probability law or stochastic continuum object should be specified.

progress.title: Stochastic homogenization extended for brittle surface functionals
progress.text: Donnarumma and Friedrich prove almost-sure stochastic homogenization for free-discontinuity surface functionals on asymptotically piecewise-rigid deformations; under ergodicity the effective density is deterministic.

progress.title: Griffith evolution homogenized in a periodic laminate
progress.text: Negri proves an effective Griffith evolution for a periodic brittle laminate with a prescribed crack path, providing a rigorous special case in which crack evolution homogenizes.

progress.title: Random fracture energies and finite-size failure separate
progress.text: Rigorous stochastic free-discontinuity homogenization establishes deterministic effective energies under ergodicity, while statistical-volume studies show that failure strength may remain strongly size-dependent and random over much larger scales.
